content.title: Kings vs. Hornets: Prediction, How to Watch for Free (3/24/26)
content.text: The Sacramento Kings (19–53) face the Charlotte Hornets (37–34) tonight at Spectrum Center in Charlotte. Charlotte enters on a three-game winning streak and is making a late push for an automatic playoff berth. Currently sitting 10th in the conference and holding the final play-in position, the Hornets trail the sixth-place Atlanta Hawks by just 2.5 games, keeping the final guaranteed postseason spot within reach with 11 games remaining. The Hornets have boosted their standing with dominant wins over the Miami Heat and Orlando Magic — teams directly ahead of them in the race — scoring at least 130 points in both contests. They followed that stretch with a convincing 124–101 victory over the Memphis Grizzlies on Saturday. Charlotte is averaging 130.0 points per game during its three-game surge, winning by an average margin of 24.0 points. Against Memphis, LaMelo Ball led the way with 29 points on 9-of-19 shooting, including seven made three-pointers, while Brandon Miller added 22 points and knocked down five shots from beyond the arc. Charlotte shot 53% from the field and 42% from deep while controlling the glass with a 49–34 rebounding advantage. Sacramento, meanwhile, comes in off a 126–122 win over the Brooklyn Nets on Sunday, its fifth victory in the last eight games. Malik Monk paced the Kings with 32 points — including 10 in the final five minutes — while Maxime Raynaud recorded a 22-point, 10-rebound double-double. Precious Achiuwa continued his strong play in the starting lineup with 14 points and 15 rebounds. Expect a blowout in this meeting between one of the league’s worst defenses and one of its most efficient offenses as of late. Final Score Prediction: Charlotte Hornets 131, Sacramento Kings 108 Injury Report Sacramento Kings Killian Hayes — Out (Left foot soreness) Precious Achiuwa — Out (Back) Nique Clifford — Out (Left mid-foot sprain) Russell Westbrook — Out (Foot) Isaiah Stevens — Day-To-Day (Right ankle soreness) Drew Eubanks — Out (Torn UCL — left thumb) Keegan Murray — Out (Ankle) De’Andre Hunter — Out (Eye surgery) Domantas Sabonis — Out (Torn left meniscus) Zach LaVine — Out (Right hand surgery) Charlotte Hornets Pat Connaughton — Day-To-Day (Illness) Tidjane Salaun — Out (Calf) Kon Knueppel — Day-To-Day (Low back soreness) How to Watch Kings vs. Hornets Tip-off for tonight’s Kings-Hornets game is set for 7:00 PM Eastern / 4:00 PM Pacific at the Spectrum Center in Charlotte. The game airs live locally on FanDuel Sports Network Southeast and NBC Sports California. Out-of-market viewers can stream the matchup on NBA League Pass for free on Amazon Prime Video with a 7-day free trial here. Amazon also offers a discounted subscription that starts at $12.74 for the first two months (then $16.99/month). The subscription also includes access to NBA TV. Fans can also choose a Team Pass to follow one team’s games for $13.99 per month.
